All code is base `R`. Every number quoted on the Session 23 slides can be reproduced here.

## Goodness of fit: Mendel's peas

```{r}
o <- c(315, 108, 101, 32)
p0 <- c(9, 3, 3, 1) / 16
sum(o) * p0                       # expected counts
g <- chisq.test(o, p = p0)
g                                  # X-squared = 0.47, df = 3, p = 0.925
qchisq(0.95, 3)                    # critical value 7.81
```

Equal plans (illustrative data): $\chi^2 = 7.96$, $\nu = 3$, $p = 0.047$.

```{r}
chisq.test(c(62, 48, 55, 35))
```

## Goodness of fit with an estimated parameter: horse kicks

```{r}
k <- c(109, 65, 22, 3, 1)                     # deaths 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 per corps-year
n <- sum(k); lambda <- sum(0:4 * k) / n       # 0.61
E <- n * c(dpois(0:1, lambda), 1 - ppois(1, lambda))   # group "2+": E_3 = 25.04
O <- c(109, 65, 26)
stat <- sum((O - E)^2 / E)
c(E, stat = stat)
pchisq(stat, df = 3 - 1 - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)       # nu = k - 1 - m = 1, p = 0.80
pchisq(stat, df = 2, lower.tail = FALSE)               # wrong df: p = 0.97
```

## Independence: hair and eye colour

```{r}
t <- margin.table(HairEyeColor, c(1, 2))
t
test <- chisq.test(t)
test                               # 138.29, df = 9
round(test$expected, 1)
round(test$stdres, 2)              # standardised residuals
sqrt(test$statistic / (sum(t) * (min(dim(t)) - 1)))    # Cramer's V = 0.28
```

## Homogeneity and the 2 x 3 table (illustrative data)

```{r}
h <- matrix(c(40, 60, 52, 48, 66, 34), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
chisq.test(h)                      # 13.6, df = 2, p = 0.0011
m <- matrix(c(30, 50, 20, 45, 40, 15), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
chisq.test(m)                      # 4.83, df = 2, p = 0.090
chisq.test(m)$expected
```

## The 2 x 2 case: z squared equals chi-square

```{r}
tab <- matrix(c(42, 58, 27, 73), 2, byrow = TRUE)
pt <- prop.test(c(42, 27), c(100, 100), correct = FALSE)
ph <- 69 / 200
z <- (0.42 - 0.27) / sqrt(ph * (1 - ph) * (2 / 100))
c(z = z, z2 = z^2, chisq = unname(chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE)$statistic))
chisq.test(tab)                    # default Yates correction: 4.34, p = 0.037
fisher.test(matrix(c(3, 1, 1, 3), 2))$p.value                       # 0.486 two-sided
fisher.test(matrix(c(3, 1, 1, 3), 2), alternative = "greater")$p.value  # 0.243
```

## Simpson's paradox: Berkeley admissions

```{r}
a <- margin.table(UCBAdmissions, c(1, 2))
prop.table(a, 2)["Admitted", ]                          # 0.445 men, 0.304 women
chisq.test(a, correct = FALSE)                          # 92.2, df = 1
round(apply(UCBAdmissions, 3, function(m) m["Admitted", ] / colSums(m)), 3)
```
